notes: REGISTER and CYCLE START now say why the cell refused them - a refused press used to vanish with no motion and no message. NC3 reads each PLC gate before pressing and names the term that shut it: robot faulted, not at perch, busy, E-stop, a job still running (DO150), manual override, beam not registered, or length. The PLC's own length check works again: NC3 writes the expected length and tolerance before registration, re-arming a compare that was silently skipped. Includes 3.9.3 - Dimetix rego position shared with the PLC (Teach / From bar), the LENGTH override following the PLC's flag, robot speed R[33] visible and settable, and the length and slip chain on the telemetry screen.
